English_display: You'll pretend to be a nobleman interested in buying some smelting works, who'd like to get a closer look at its operation.

English_display: It's exactly a hundred corves altogether… and now it's getting interesting.

English_display: Buresh is a very cautious and clever man. I reckon he won't be happy to have someone snooping around his property.

English_display: He's the slyest fox of them all. He comes from somewhere in Moravia, and he moved to Kuttenberg a few years ago.

English_display: You're lucky I found out myself how many corves it was.

English_display: You're just lucky I managed to learn from all the pitmen how much they extracted.

English_display: Be quiet, would you?! I'll remember your actions.

English_display: I reckon he won't be thrilled, but he won't turn you down.

English_display: You must come to him dressed to the nines and act impeccably, so as not to arouse the slightest suspicion!

English_display: But be careful! We don't want anyone to find out what we're looking for.

English_display: Apparently, they extracted a little over thirty corves on the feast of St. Petronilla.

English_display: If my guess is correct, it should be ninety. It still doesn't prove anything, but at least it'll give us a clue.

English_display: If silver is going missing, it must be happening in the smelting works. That's where the ten unreported corves disappeared!

English_display: If you don't have anything of the sort, visit a tailor in town. I'm sure he can sell you something nice.

English_display: In short, be charismatic! As charismatic as you can manage!

English_display: Try looking around the smelting works in Grund, see if anyone knows anything. Just don't draw too much attention to yourself.

English_display: I'd only end up with my head on the chopping block, and I don't even want to think about what they'd do to Rosa!

English_display: If Sigismund were to find out, he'd have him executed at once, regardless of his noble blood!

English_reference: I wish I did. Sorry.
English_display: I wish I did... Sorry.

English_reference: Strain that through linen and add a bit of honeycomb and a drop of tung oil.
English_display: Strain that through a cloth and add a bit of honeycomb as well as a drop of wood oil.

English_reference: Well, he was going to go all the way to Kolin on some business, but he didn't get there.
English_display: Well, I know he was headed to Kolin on business, but he never made it there.

English_reference: I've told the women before, but they don't listen to me.
English_display: I already gave the women some advice, but they just don't listen to me.

English_reference: Finally, they need to cut up a black chicken along its backbone and put it on Peter's forehead.
English_display: Finally, they need to cut open a black chicken along its backbone and put it on Peter's forehead.

English_reference: I wouldn't be surprised if Peter got jumped by some bandits on the road.
English_display: I wouldn't be surprised if some bandit grabbed him by the throat along the way.

English_display: I've no idea what happened to him there. Maybe his horse got spooked, or his dog bit him...? I just don't know.

English_reference: I don't know exactly when it started. But I remember that Peter was to take the goods all the way to Petschkau.
English_display: I don't remember exactly when. But I do remember that Peter was transporting goods all the way to Petschkau.

English_reference: Everything I could think of, I told Mlada already. It was useless.
English_display: I already told Mlada everything I could think of. Nothing worked.

English_reference: They should put that up his arse.
English_display: Then all they have to do is wash his arse out with it.

English_reference: Peter is going mad and this is the only thing that can help him.
English_display: Peter is going mad, and this is the only thing that can help him.

English_reference: Peter's just losing his marbles.
English_display: Simply put, Peter's losing his marbles.

English_reference: I picked some herbs for Mlada and left them in the room. That's all I can do for them.
English_display: I picked some herbs for Mlada and left them in the room. That's about all I can do for them.

English_reference: Then they should mix mallow, linseed, bran and a pinch of salt and boil it in a cup of water.
English_display: Then they should mix mallow, linseed, bran and a pinch of salt and boil it in water.

English_reference: But first they must shave his head.
English_display: But before that, they'll have to shave his head.

English_reference: It came so suddenly.
English_display: It came over him so suddenly.

English_reference: Trust me, this is the only thing that's gonna help him.
English_display: Trust me, this is the only thing that's going to help him.

English_reference: Um… Actually, none of us here know what to do.
English_display: Hmm… Honestly, none of us here knows what to do.

English_reference: No. Or maybe if you looked in his workshop, perhaps you could think of something…
English_display: No. Unless… maybe you could look around his workshop. You might pick up some clue.

English_reference: He came back all red, couldn't breathe, he was like someone tried to hang him.
English_display: He came back all red, couldn't breathe, as if he was being hanged.

English_reference: Then he went to bed and since then… He's just lying there, doesn't eat, potions aren't helping.
English_display: Then he went to bed, and since then he's… just been lying there. He doesn't eat, not even the potions are helping.

English_reference: But he came back empty-handed, breathless and flustered.
English_display: But he came back empty-handed, breathless and confused.

English_reference: It's as if he was keeping secrets from me, or protecting me from something.
English_display: It's as if he was keeping secrets from me, or maybe just protecting me from something.

English_display: My husband doesn't travel outside the village often. This last time he had some business in Petschkau near Kolin.

English_reference: I can't. I'm desperate, too.
English_display: I can't. I'm desperate myself.

English_reference: He doesn't sleep at night. Or at least I think so.
English_display: He doesn't sleep a wink at night. At least I don't think he does.

English_reference: He's been confused for a couple of days, spending time in the workshop, but he didn't work. God only knows what he was doing in there.
English_display: He was fumbling around here for a few days, not doing his job, just spending time in his workshop. Lord knows what he was doing in there.

English_reference: Peter's just a regular cooper. We've lived here for years, we go to church.
English_display: Peter is just an ordinary cooper. We've lived here for years, we go to church.

English_reference: If I didn't sleep as well, our homestead would fall apart.
English_display: If I stopped sleeping too, our homestead would fall apart.

English_reference: I've tried, well, everything.
English_display: I've tried just about everything…

English_reference: You try that. He doesn't want to talk to me about anything.
English_display: Try that. He won't speak to me about anything.

English_reference: Eve? She's scared of him like a cat is scared of a dog. She's not stupid enough to do that…
English_display: Eva? She is afraid of him like the devil of the cross. She's not that stupid.

English_reference: We'll get to that. There's a rumour at a roadside pub that his woman cheated on him!
English_display: We'll get to that. There's a rumour at the inn that his wife cheated on him!

English_reference: That chap's a goner. As I know the butcher, he'll want blood. And poor Eve will likely also get the beating of her life.
English_display: That chap's a goner. Knowing the butcher, he'll want blood. And poor Eva will likely also get the beating of her life.

English_reference: Just so. But work won't wait. Farewell!
English_display: Aye. But work won't wait. Farewell!

English_reference: Stupid? Certainly not. She had it arranged nicely so the butcher wouldn't catch her.
English_display: Stupid? Certainly not. She arranged it nicely so the butcher wouldn't catch her.

English_display: Are you surprised? With the rumours going round?

English_reference: From who?
English_display: From who, may I ask?

English_display: You don't know what you're talking about! Eva is an honest woman. She married a brute, but she is as loyal to him as a dog!

English_reference: It's a disgrace! To cheat on her husband with some vagabond.
English_display: It's a disgrace! To cheat on her husband… and with some vagabond.

English_reference: You mean Eve, the butcher's wife?
English_display: You mean Eva, the butcher's wife?

English_display: Poor Eva. I know her well and I'd put my neck on the line that she didn't do anything.

English_display: There won't be anything here, I’ll move on.

English_display: Besides the cows, I found some beer too. It was locked up in one of your people's cellar.

English_reference: At one of your people's houses I found several barrels of beer in the cellar.
English_display: I found a few barrels of beer in one of your people's cellar.

English_reference: A spoke to him in the Devil's Den, but I lost sight of him along the way…
English_display: I spoke to him in the Devil's Den, but I lost sight of him along the way…

English_display: The arrow isn't magic. Karel just got lucky, and that shot to the head just scrambled his brain!

English_display: Keep it as a relic. That way, Karel will always be with you, as well as the blessing he received.

English_display: No! It will endow me with great power and then I'll lead my companions to abundance and plenty.

English_display: That's just like him! I give him a simple task, and he still manages to fuck it up!

English_display: Aye, couldn't hurt to go for an ale. What do you say, Henry?

English_display: But you're reet. I didn't think it'd be so hard to hang up a shitty pair of braies.

English_display: For sure! A canny job, kiddar!

English_display: Easy, Franzi, you could have tried yourself, couldn't ye?

English_display: You're reet, now would be an good time to get off the streets. The Saints would never dare to come into our tavern.

English_display: Marras, man, here we say "marras"!

English_display: No bother, it's alang the way. Besides, we'd better get off the street for a while.

English_display: Jesus! What kind of a gowk are you?

English_display: What the… what's the matter?

English_display: Hm, that's possible. But it was well worth the laugh.

English_display: It just didn't work out. What can you do?

English_display: Well get gannin' before someone notices us and tattles to the Saints!

English_display: All done, the braies are getting an airing…

English_display: But they saw me at the tavern.

English_display: To hell with the stinking braies, there's no way I can get up there.

English_display: So I'm back from the tavern, mates.

English_display: Not for now, maybe, but it's just a matter of time before the Saints find out and come after us.

English_display: There might be something interesting here, but no pearl mussels.

English_display: What about you? Are you looking forward to the tournament coming up?

English_display: And in the meantime, let's enjoy the tournament!

English_display: I mean, this is a royal city, isn't it?

English_display: I reckon you're right, I wouldn't want to embarrass myself in front of everyone.

English_display: I hope there won't be any trouble… Those nobles can be awfully irritable…

English_display: A new dress, eh? I reckon I should get something too. I hope I have enough groschen left over.

English_display: I've been taking lessons at the fechthalle, and I've learned quite a bit already.

English_display: His name is… bloody hell, what was it? Zdenyek? Zbyshek? Something starting with a Z.

English_display: Aye. I reckon I'll have a look first, and maybe next time I'll even fight.

English_display: Konrad wins every time. Just look at him, he could cut you in half without even pulling his sword from the scabbard!

English_reference: Between you and me, we're not.
English_display: Between you and me, we surely aren't.

English_display: Well? Come to your senses yet?

English_display: True enough, but you know how it is with the kings these days… one is captured, and the other set up an army camp just outside the town.

English_display: He sews like a master, but he's still just a journeyman, so you'll also get a better price.

English_display: Nobles hold tournaments all the time, so why not us? Between you and me, are we really any worse than they are?

English_display: I heard about this one bloke. A young fellah, but they say no one stands a chance against him. Because he's in league with the devil!

English_display: They say he soaks his prick in rooster blood before every fight, that it gives him super-human strength!

English_display: Then let's just hope the lords don't take offense.

English_display: That city tournament… What an occasion, eh? Will you go?

English_reference: Me too.

English_display: That sort of talk is dangerous. The tournament's supposed to be a celebration of the city, and all that swordfighting is just a bit of fun, that's all.

English_display: These days, we need to rely on ourselves. The lords won't protect us…

English_reference: Try Green Vendelin, he'll find the time to make you something nice.
English_display: Try Green Venda, I'm sure he'll find the time to make you something nice.

English_display: You should, even the city council is going to be at the tournament. Like I said, a grand event. One has to be mindful of their appearance.

English_reference: We deserve to have some fun. And the town tournament will be just that. I'm really looking forward to it.
English_display: We deserve to have some fun. And the city tournament will be just that. I'm really looking forward to it.

English_reference: Sorry, I didn't mean it. I'm bit mistrustful, that's all.
English_display: Sorry, I didn't mean it. I'm a bit mistrustful, that's all.

English_display: Really?! You've made my day. Here, take this! A little reward for that good news.

English_display: Well, just don't head straight down the hill here, go around instead. It's a bit further, but at least you'll avoid that bloody barn.

English_display: Some vagabond has camped there. On the booze from morning till night. A right nuisance, he is.

English_display: I spent most of my time with the vomiting one, or out in the yard scrubbing his bedding. I didn’t see anyone…

English_reference: Not exactly helpful, I know. Any idea when that was?
English_display: It's not exactly helpful, I know. Any idea when that was?

English_display: Someone went through our room... or rather tossed it all about. Likely looking for something.

English_display: I understand. Even so, thanks for your help.

English_reference: Good.

English_display: You're supposed to tell me where I can find the supplies for the king.

English_display: Well that's too bad, because this is definitely not going to be enough.

English_display: I'm collecting supplies for the king's men. Do you have them ready?

English_display: They're here, right next to the door to the cottage.

English_display: It's all we have! The next harvest isn't for a long time.

English_display: Where do you think? Right behind the door in the cottage! Everything's ready underneath the window.

English_display: We don't, you've already taken everything else.

English_display: It's all I have. I swear to God! We're poor. We've already given more than we could!

English_display: When you pass through the gate to the yard, you'll see them on your right.

English_reference: Right behind the door, everything's ready to go! Leaning against the wall.
English_display: Right behind the door, leaning against the wall. Everything's ready to go!

English_display: It's all I have, you already took everything else!

English_display: And sometimes they are more likely to burn me at the stake just for being different.

English_display: And if you want something a bit less ordinary, it is: Kaj djas, more?

English_display: While we have no master, just the sun and God above us and the grass beneath our feet.

English_display: And why do you not settle down, instead of jumping from the frying pan into the fire, gadjo?

English_display: May cholera strike him down, the scoundrel!

English_display: But that is only said by men to men, mind you! We women say: So taves, mri chay?

English_display: Black magic is a path every honest manush avoids like the plague.

English_reference: !T Ay, gadjo, but from God!
English_display: Yay, gadjo. From God, of course!

English_display: What do you mean, over and over? There is the east road and west road, too, right?

English_display: Ah, I see. Well, in the winter we are always in the south, and in the summer we go north.

English_display: If you have faith, then it will work.

English_display: Ko tuke p-hendja? What magic, gadjo?

English_display: Laches gadjo, mishtes. What can an old woman like me do for you?

English_display: We live our lives as if each day could be the last, that is all!

English_display: Oy Devla miro! Of course, the good kind that helps and comes from God.

English_display: So hin chachipen andro dzhivipen?

English_display: There are all kinds, but if you want to say "How are you?", then it is "Sar tuke djal?"

English_display: My old Ma, though, may she rest in peace, she knew all kinds of things!

English_display: You guessed it, gadjo. We do not know and we do not want to know. God always takes care of his children.

English_display: You know, gadjo, nothing and everything...

English_display: Simple. Black magic is only used for the selfish benefit of fools who think only of themselves.

English_display: It is always different. Sometimes the womenfolk could kiss my feet when I cure their pains…

English_display: Even Lord Kuno himself said he would welcome you in his retinue.

English_display: Fürs Geld oder für die Freude: for money or for joy.

English_display: That's the motto of our Lord, Sir Urso von Morgenstern and it's quite fitting for mercenaries like us, don't you think?

English_reference: What's it to you? Do we know each other?
English_display: What's it to you who I am?

English_reference: Come back to me when you're ready to wager some coin on your shooting skills. Not before.
English_display: Come back to me when you're ready to wager some coin on your shooting. Not before.

English_reference: Listen, Henry, did you come to shoot?
English_display: Look here, Henry, did you come to shoot?

English_reference: That's all we need is someone wandering around von Bergow's quarry...
English_display: That's all we need, fellahs wandering around Lord von Bergow's quarry.

English_reference: But you were with them. I don't care about all the rest. Maybe it could've turned out worse and maybe it didn't because of you, but…
English_display: But you were still with them, that's all that matters. Maybe it could've turned out worse, and maybe it didn't thanks to you, but…

English_reference: I reckon so… We kept expecting soldiers to bang on our doors, but nothing happened… So we got used to it.
English_display: I suppose so… We kept expecting soldiers to show up banging on our doors, but nothing ever happened. So we got used to it.

English_reference: We were faring well, but now… Times are tough.
English_display: We were doing alright, but now… Times are tough.

English_reference: Maybe we won't rest In peace even then and they'll murder us as a farewell.
English_display: And maybe not even then. Maybe they'll come and murder us as a farewell.

English_reference: It wasn't… And maybe we owe you our lives, but we won't rest easy until those brigands pull out of here, and even then…
English_display: It wasn't… And maybe we owe you our lives, but we won't rest easy until those brigands pull out of here.

English_reference: Why do you ask? You left something here, so we might not die of hunger.
English_display: Why do you ask? You left us with some food, so maybe we won't even starve to death.

English_reference: That certainly didn't help, especially the army camping on our doorstep.
English_display: That surely didn't help, especially with that army camp on our doorstep.

English_reference: Whenever they decide to replenish their supplies, they stop here. If they show up here again, they'll take what they want and I'm not sure we won't die of hunger.
English_display: Whenever they need to restock their supplies, they come here. If they show up here again and take what they want, I don't think we'll survive much longer.

English_reference: Whenever I see you, my heart is like to burst.
English_display: Whenever I see you, it's like a knife in my heart.

English_reference: For you, my friend, always.
English_display: For you, anytime, my friend.

English_reference: Please, just call me by my name. No need for formalities. Titles are pointless.
English_display: No, there's no need for formalities. Titles are worthless.

English_reference: Indeed. My name is Bartoschek of Drahonitz. My father served Emperor Charles his entire life.
English_display: Indeed. I'm Bartoschek of Drahonitz. My father served Emperor Charles his entire life.

English_reference: While travelling, a band of scoundrels lied in wait for us, and nearly got us.
English_display: A band of scoundrels was lying in wait for us on the road, and they nearly got us.

English_reference: You see, you need to earn your name, not just inherit it along with a silver spoon.
English_display: A man should earn a name for himself. It's not enough to be born with a silver spoon in your mouth.

English_reference: And I didn't have any, so I had to do what I was best at.
English_display: And I didn't have one, so I had to do what I do best.

English_reference: As I say, thank the Virgin Mary and all the saints for standing by our side.
English_display: Like I say, I thank the Virgin Mary and all the saints for watching over us.

English_reference: I reckon you could say that. Not long ago I won two big tournaments, so I was invited to a very fine feast.
English_display: Depends what you mean. I'd recently won two big tournaments, so I was invited to a splendid banquet.

English_reference: He's a man of principle and a true master of the long sword.
English_display: He's a man of honour, and a peerless master of the longsword.

English_reference: That's simple. I was serving in the garrison at Prague's royal castle, where von Bergow was a frequent guest.
English_display: That's simple. I was serving in the garrison in Prague's royal castle, where von Bergow was a frequent guest.

English_reference: We all seem to go our own ways. I even studied at University, when I could afford it.
English_display: We each have our own path, it seems. I even studied at university, while I could still afford it.

English_reference: It might have come down to a single fool's mistake, I don’t know. But if they would have waited just a bit longer, we wouldn't have stood a chance.
English_display: It might have come down to a single fool's mistake, I don't know. But if they'd just waited a bit longer, we wouldn't have stood a chance.

English_reference: I may come from a noble family, but we are not famous or rich, and studying costs loads of money.
English_display: I may come from a noble family, but we're not renowned or rich, and studying costs a fortune.

English_reference: I must say, it was well thought out. They nearly got us.
English_display: It was well planned, I must admit. They nearly got us.

English_reference: Fortunately, today there are enough swordsmen in Prague who will instruct you for money.
English_display: Fortunately, these days there are plenty of swordsmen in Prague who'll train you for coin.

English_reference: I had already heard of Trosky, but it was one of those things were you don't believe it until you see it with your own eyes.
English_display: I'd heard of Trosky, of course, but I was still astonished when I saw it with my own eyes.

English_reference: Sir Otto van Bergow hired me in Prague as his personal guard and as fencing master for the local castle garrison.
English_display: Sir Otto hired me in Prague as his bodyguard and a swordmaster for the local castle garrison.

English_reference: If you really want to hear what I think about it, then I'd say those miscreants weren't acting in unison. They were rushing things.
English_display: If you really want to know what I think, the idiots lacked discipline. They rushed it.

English_reference: Ha! I wouldn't say that. I do dabble in a bit of poetry, but that's all.
English_display: Ha! I wouldn't go that far. I dabble in poetry a bit, that's all.

English_reference: That's right. You know, I was there for every fight at University and managed to survive, so I thought, "This is what I'm good at."
English_display: That's right. I spent more time fighting than studying at university and came out of it alive, so I reckoned that's where my talent lies.

English_reference: Of course it's just a nickname, because of my ink-black hair. Every swordsman has one, you know.
English_display: It's just a nickname, of course, because of my black hair. Every swordsman has a nickname, you know.

English_reference: He probably already sensed he was in danger, and he was right…
English_display: I reckon he sensed he was in danger, and he was right.

English_reference: I'd like to hear your question, Henry.
English_display: Ask away, Henry.

English_reference: It was there that Sir Otto requested my services at his castle.
English_display: It was there Sir Otto offered me a position at his castle.

English_reference: That's hard to say. Perhaps we were just lucky, and God was by our side.
English_display: Hard to say. Maybe we were just lucky, and God was watching over us.

English_reference: If you do, go and see Master Lamprecht of Prague and send him my greetings.
English_display: If you do, go and see Master Lamprecht and give him my regards.

English_reference: I have dedicated the last five years of my life to that art. I have travelled and been taught by several masters.
English_display: I've dedicated the last five years of my life to it. I travelled a lot and was taught by several masters.

English_reference: Well, I haven't been that far away either, friend, but one cannot become a master without knowing true masters.
English_display: Well, I haven't been all that far either, but unless you learn from true masters, you'll never become a master yourself.

English_reference: ... And keep going until you reach the forest. You'll see their wagons there.
English_display: And keep going till you reach the forest. You'll see their wagons there.

English_reference: But once the construction was completed, we only work for von Semin.
English_display: But since the job's been done, we only cut for Lord Semine.

English_reference: Before we cut hard wood for the construction works in Trosky.
English_display: Before we was cutting hard timber for the building works in Trosky.

English_reference: It's misery. The trees in the rocks are as twisted as a pig's tail. They're worth the least.
English_display: It's misery. The trees in the rocks are as twisted as a pig's tail. There's bugger all coin in felling them.

English_reference: It's easy, just follow the road from von Semin's to the West until the end of that long meadow...
English_display: It's easy, just follow the road from Semine to the west till the end of that long meadow...

English_reference: But I've been around and I think it'll soon backfire on him!
English_display: But I've seen a thing or two and I reckon it'll come back to haunt him!

English_reference: How do you think? I try to keep my eye on them so that they don't get in my way here.
English_display: How do you think? I try to keep an eye on them so's they don't get under my feet here.

English_display: He gets a bit of coin in the town for it, but I say them local pine tree is miserable wood for building.

English_reference: Old von Semin is a kind man and he keeps a protective hand over them.
English_display: Old Lord Semine's a good-hearted gent and he keeps a protective hand over them.

English_reference: Eh, we really are living in uncertain times.
English_display: These truly are troubling times we're living in…

English_display: The silverworks are the heart of Grund. I can't imagine what would happen if they were to shut down.

English_reference: Aye, I pray it'll be some honest Christian and not some profiteer.
English_display: Aye, I pray it'll be some honest Christian, and not some profiteer.

English_reference: Aye, aye... Sometimes someone fights in the tavern, but I reckon that happens everywhere and it's actually a good thing.
English_display: Aye, aye... Sometimes someone gets into a scrap in the tavern, but I reckon that happens everywhere. It might actually be a good thing.

English_display: There is great uncertainty here now. People are worried about what's going to happen now that Buresh died so suddenly.

English_display: But if you are interested in local history, you should go and see the scribe Erazim, he's been here the longest.

English_display: In Trosky we only have the chapel in the castle tower.

English_display: What can I tell you? Lord Von Bergow provides a livelihood for many people.

English_display: And the ruler of the roost here is the chamberlain, Ulrich von Schaumberg. You seriously don't want to cross him, lad!

English_reference: And then suddently he falls from the tower? I heard someone helped him, but in my opinion… it was suicide!
English_display: And then suddenly he falls from the tower? I heard someone may have "helped" him, but in my opinion, it was suicide!

English_reference: But that, lad, is absolutely none of your business!
English_display: But that, young man, is absolutely none of your business!

English_reference: Even that odd gravedigger didn't want to bury him. And they made perform his service!
English_display: Even that odd gravedigger didn't want to bury him. And they made me say the service for him!

English_reference: The Lord's ways have led me all the way down here.
English_display: The Lord's path has led me all the way down here.

English_reference: He's the royal Sub-Chamberlain, and politics takes up a lot of his time.
English_display: He's the Royal Chamberlain, and politics takes up a lot of his time.

English_reference: It's true, you'll find the closest one in Uyezd or in Mladeyov on the other side...
English_display: It's true, you'll find the closest one in Ujezd or in Mladyeov on the other side...

English_reference: She is a pious woman, but also bloody firm and strict on the servants!
English_display: She's a pious woman, but also damned firm and strict on the servants!

English_reference: But numbers and accounts aren't everything. One should also think about the salvation of his own soul!
English_display: But numbers and accounts aren't everything. One should also think about the salvation of one's soul!

English_reference: Now I'm back with my people in the village. Like when I was a lad.
English_display: Now I'm back in the village with my people, just like when I was a lad.

English_reference: Their problems are much different than those of the lords, and honestly… it's refreshing.
English_display: Their problems are very different from those of the lords, and honestly… it's refreshing.

English_reference: Well, it's been a few years, for certain...
English_display: Well, it's been quite a few years…

English_reference: Well… at least I don't have to walk up all those stairs to get to the castle chapel, eh?
English_display: Well… at least I don't have to walk up all those stairs to get to the castle chapel every day, eh?

English_reference: Plus, his Hetman Thomas is responsible for the safety of Sir Otto.
English_display: Then Captain Thomas is responsible for Sir Otto's security.

English_reference: ... And yet he spends most of his time in Prague.
English_display: And yet he spends most of his time in Prague.

English_reference: He's an old soldier and a fair bloke, even if he doesn't come to confession as the year is long.
English_display: He's an old soldier and an upright fellow, even if he doesn't come to confession more than once a year.

English_reference: Well, pay attention mainly to the Lady Yitka, she's the wife of our Burgrave Hashek.
English_display: Then you should watch out especially for Lady Jitka. She's the wife of our Burgrave Hashek.

English_reference: That's not what I said! The old Chamberlain Ulrich manages the estate, and he's definitely good with numbers.
English_display: That's not what I said! The old chamberlain, Ulrich, manages the estate, and he's definitely good with numbers at least…

English_reference: He scared me, honestly. He wanted me to bless his armour… his sword, even… Lord von Bergow never wanted such things from me.
English_display: He scared me, to be frank. He wanted me to bless his armour… his sword, even… Lord von Bergow never wanted such things from me.

English_reference: Simply put, this region is the middle of nowhere. Great things only started to happen with the arrival of Sir Otto von Bergow.
English_display: In short, this domain is the middle of nowhere. It was only with Sir Otto's arrival that great things started happening.

English_reference: !P Diese ganze Mannschaft including the horses belong to Sir Urso.
English_display: Die ganze Truppe including the horses belong to Sir Urso.

English_reference: !P Entschuldigung, mein Freund, but you'd better talk about that with mein Herr von Morgenstern.
English_display: Entschuldigung, mein Freund, but you'd better talk about that with Herr von Morgenstern.

English_reference: !P Fur gutes Geld oder aus gutem Grund.
English_display: Fürs Geld oder für die Freude.

English_reference: !P Ganz wie Sie wollen...
English_display: Ganz, wie du willst …

English_reference: !P Ja, ich weiss, wer Sie sind... Brabant spoke to my lord, Sir Urso about you.
English_display: Ja, ich weiß, wer du bist... Brabant spoke to my lord, Sir Urso about you.

English_reference: !P Macht nichts, das ist egal... A war is meant to be fought, especially if you pay us well.
English_display: Macht nichts, das ist egal... A war is meant to be fought, especially if you pay us well.

English_reference: !P He said you want to do something big. Was ist hier los?
English_display: He said you want to do something big. Worum geht es denn?

English_display: It's not all Sigismund's fault. The councillors have been putting off the repairs for years now.

English_reference: And I'm not going to freeze up in the tower like this in the summer.
English_display: And I am not going to sit up there in the tower freezing my arse off.

English_reference: !P Das stimmt, actually so it isn't lost! These days people will steal anything that isn't nailed down.
English_display: Das stimmt, actually so it isn't lost! These days people will steal anything that isn't nailed down.

English_reference: !P Ja das wurde reichen, but the Monastery Gate is the seat of the command of the city guard.
English_display: Ja, das würde reichen, but the monastery gate is the seat of the command of the city guard.

English_reference: And city construction attracts those swinish thieves like flies on shit.
English_display: And construction sites like these attract bloody thieves like flies to shit.

English_reference: !P Genau, too late, but there's something else behind it...
English_display: Genau, too late, but there's something else behind it...

English_reference: Plus, as the commander I'm obliged to train the city militia and the lads from my watch.
English_display: Plus, as the commander, it is my duty to train the city militia, as well as the lads from my watch.

English_reference: They’re not, it's more of a repair… Maybe you have already noticed that our city's bulwarks have suffered considerable damage.
English_display: Not building, more like repairing… You may have noticed the city's defenses suffered considerable damage.

English_reference: Ever since Sigismund replaced the city counsel, the new bürgermeister has been bending over backwards to get people to like him.
English_display: Ever since Sigismund replaced the city council, the new Burgermeister has been bending over backwards to get people to like him.

English_reference: So there are  repairs, construction, even St Barbara's Church is growing right in front of our eyes.
English_display: So there are repairs, construction, even St. Barbara's Church is growing right in front of our eyes.

English_reference: Unfortunately, he left to take of some things in Moravia a month ago, and hasn't yet returned.
English_display: Unfortunately, he left to take care of some things in Moravia a month ago, and hasn't yet returned.

English_reference: Let me tell you, I hope we go back to Hochwarth soon. Every since the knight Florian started circling around Adleta, I don't have a moment's rest.
English_display: Let me tell you, I hope we go back to Hochwarth soon. Every since the knight Florian started circling around Adleta, I haven't a moment's rest.

English_display: I brought here some of the Lord of Hochwarth's men at arms, at the request of our Sir Otto.

English_display: So I have to stand in for him, as well as protect his youngest daughter, Adleta, who insisted on joining us for the journey.

English_reference: Oof, you have no idea what sort of troubles the girl causes me. She's used to having things her way and it's driving me mad!
English_display: Ah, you have no idea the sort of bother that lass gives me. She's used to having everything her way and it's driving me mad!

English_reference: !P Also gut, was ist los?
English_display: Also gut, was gibt es denn?

English_display: Oh, yes, as soon as he got here. But my men know what to do. Mit der Hilfe Gottes, we fended him off and forced him to negotiate.

English_display: Der Teufel soll Sigismund holen!

English_display: Ach, so Gott will, these evil times will soon be over.

English_display: Schön, dann frag nur.

English_display: Dann pass mal auf! As soon as the soldiers began looting the villages around the city, the local nobility quickly decided it's better to pay them Lösegeld.

English_reference: !P Ja, genau das ist es...
English_display: Das trifft den Nagel auf den Kopf …

English_display: Why should he pay them out of his own pocket when the local lords are feeding them?

English_reference: !P Mein Herr Peter, however, had to pay him a fat Losegeld to leave us in peace.
English_display: Mein Herr Peter, however, had to pay him a fat Lösegeld to leave us in peace.

English_display: They've occupied the hill above the main road near Kuttenberg, so no one could just come and help the town.

English_reference: The villages in the vicinity fared even worse…
English_display: The villages in the vicinity fared even worse.

English_display: Wie bitte? Hast du den Verstand verloren? You can forget about that, you won't get in there!

English_display: Diese Banditenbanden have settled in there... A bunch of dossers who'll easily cut your throat for a piece of bread!

English_display: They are. Diese dreckigen Hurensöhne are angry, you see! They thought they would rake in the silver from the Kuttenberg mines.

English_display: Das ist nicht schwer, you just take the main road to the east and then you'll see the church towers.

English_display: Sir George, who previously owned the armour, wanted to have a nice poleaxe made in Prague too, but he died of the plague before he could do it.

English_reference: Because he didn't have any choice, my friend! He never found the armour here!
English_display: Because he didn't have any choice, my friend! He never found the armour!

English_display: It is said that George the Lion of Wartenberg brought it here. He was the nephew of Lord Chenyek of Wartenberg, who built Trosky.

English_reference: No need to worry much about it, it's just an old wives' tale.
English_display: Don't worry too much about it, it's just an old wives' tale.

English_reference: That is, for Brunswick, not for Ludmila's new groom. But the lion took care of him.
English_display: For Brunswick that is, not so for Ludmila's new groom. But the lion took care of that.

English_display: This George spent a lot of time with King Wenceslas. A suspiciously long amount of time, if you know what I mean.

English_reference: You too, lad. And keep an eye on that armour! You know what they say, easy come easy go.
English_display: You too, lad. And keep an eye on that armour! You know what they say, easy come, easy go.

English_display: As a reward, Wenceslas gave young Wartenberg the name Lion and the armour of his ancestor, Prince Brunswick.

English_display: That will do, let me see what we're working with.

English_display: It's lucky that you happen to ask!

English_display: And anyway, we're in mourning, we're in no mood for fighting the Zhelejovites…

English_display: Alright, but don't get your hopes up… And don't you go ganging up with them Zhelejov bastards against us!

English_reference: Is that even possible? Olbram will never drop it. He says the whole pasture is his!
English_display: Chance'd be a fine thing! Olbram will never give up. He says the whole pasture is his!

English_display: We'll sort it all out with them there. Nicely, man to man. Wouldn't you like to join us?

English_reference: The border is by the orchard, that'th where I got my arthe beat!
English_display: The border'th by the orthard, that'th where I got my arthe kicked!

English_display: There's no one to join, unfortunately… Didn't you hear? The region is in mourning. We put off the fight with the Zhelejovites for now.

English_reference: You certainly won't be joining us! Not after what you've done.
English_display: You sure won't be joining us! Not after what you've done.

English_display: Thrush? He already said ages ago he doesn't want to get involved. He even threatened us with the stocks if we keep bothering him!

English_display: We're planning to meet with the Zhelejovites in the pasture that they keep arguing with us about.

English_reference: Pfuj! Who knows what the old coot got beaten for back then…
English_display: Pah! Who knows what the old fool got his arse kicked for back then!

English_reference: Do you think I'm stupid?
English_display: Do you think I'm daft?

English_reference: We'll get into a huge argument and then beat each other's arses…
English_display: We'll get into a huge argument and then start punching each other in the gob!

English_display: You could not! And if I was you, I'd get out of here quick. We've no love for Olbram's bootlickers around here…

English_reference: You team up with the Zhelejovites against us and now you come over like nothing happened? Fuck off back to Olbram!
English_display: You team up with the Zhelejovites against us, and now you come here like nothing happened? Piss off back to Olbram!

English_reference: Yeah, talking...
English_display: Aye, talk…

English_display: So, then? Should I send for Olbram so we can get going?

English_display: Alright, fine. But don't dawdle!

English_display: That's what I like to hear! Come, let's get the lads together and get going!

English_reference: Are you yanking my pizzle? You run off to make trouble in our village, and now you want to come with us to the pasture, eh? No way! Get out of here!
English_display: Are you yanking my pizzle? You run off to make trouble in our village, and now you want to come with us to the pasture, eh? Not a chance! Get lost!

English_display: Now? Damn it Henry, that won't do. The region's in mourning, nobody's in the mood for arguments. The fight with the Zhelejovites is off…

English_reference: Do you think I'm stupid or what? I know you teamed up with Olbram against us!  Go ahead and tell him we're not going to have any conflicts with them!
English_display: Do you think I'm daft or something? I know you teamed up with Olbram against us! Go ahead and tell him we ain't sorting anything out with them!

English_reference: Pray the Lord's Prayer, press your palms together and with all your strength ask God for forgiveness!
English_display: Recite the Lord's Prayer, clasp your palms together with all your strength and ask God for forgiveness!

English_display: Say the Lord's Prayer, and you will be forgiven.

English_display: Not far from Horschan, Perun's Spring, as the locals call it, gushes from the ground.

English_display: I'm not at all pleased with the heathen name. We must prove that it has no other meaning than that which comes from Christ, our Saviour.

English_display: Bless yourself and say the Lord's Prayer.

English_display: Isn't it beautiful? Finally a wedding that will be long remembered in these parts!

English_display: Chance'd be a fine thing!

English_display: Of course, you might regret it in the morning.

English_display: Aye... well, thanks. And you'll drink to it with me?

English_reference: To my daughter and her happiness!
English_display: To my lass and her happiness!

English_display: That means first winning against Radovan the blacksmith, Emmerich the apothecary and Ulrich the chamberlain!

English_reference: Don't complain. You can win a badge from them too.
English_display: Don't complain. You can win badges from them too.

English_display: So...? All badges are good.

English_display: Easy, youngster, it's not that simple. You have to earn that chance!

English_display: Have you come to play dice?

English_reference: Someone's feeling lucky...
English_display: Someone's feeling lucky!

English_display: A person makes his own luck.

English_display: Asking a bit much, aren't you?

English_display: I'm happy to hear that. Here's to my Agnes!

English_reference: God, you're such a bore.
English_display: God, you're straight-laced!

English_reference: I’m glad to hear it. But it doesn’t make sense any more today, unless you want to drive in the dark.
English_display: I'm glad to hear it. But it's too late now, it's getting dark.

English_reference: Do you know what a slog it is burning a whole village? But so what, we have food. And now you clear off and next time learn to come on time, so you don’t miss all the fun!
English_display: Do you know what a slog it is burning down a whole village? But never mind, at least we have food. Now clear off! Next time show up on time, or you'll miss all the fun!

English_reference: Let’s get going then, so we’re back nice and early.
English_display: Let's get going then, so we're back nice and early.

English_reference: Me, and they usually send some Cumans with me, because people are afraid of them.
English_display: Me, and they usually send some Cumans along, because people are afraid of them.

English_reference: Are they already running out of men that they're sending such little ones?
English_display: Are they running out of blokes, sending a milksop like you?

English_reference: What kind of fucking soldier are you? If I wasn’t in dire need of men, I’d send you back to the countryside where you belong.
English_display: What kind of a fucking soldier are you?! If I wasn't so low on men, I'd send you back to the shithole you came from!

English_reference: Do you think that the army will just wait until the gentleman graces us with his presence? Fuck that, laddie!
English_display: Do you think the army will just wait until the gentleman graces us with his presence? Fuck that, lad!

English_reference: But don't worry. I’ve already sent a couple of blokes ahead to get everything ready. That’ll be enough for that riffraff.
English_display: But don't worry. I already sent a couple of blokes ahead to get everything ready. I reckon they can handle a few peasants.

English_reference: But get a move on. I won’t be waiting here for you forever!
English_display: But get a move on. We're not going to wait forever!

English_reference: Don’t mollycoddle me, lad.  You got drunk and lost all track of time with a bathmaid, eh?
English_display: Don't lie to me, lad! You got pissed and lost track of time with a bathwench, didn't you?

English_reference: They will, but fuck all good it’ll do them. We’ll chase them out of their houses, bring the cart to the village green and take whatever we can.
English_display: They will, but fuck all good it'll do them. We'll chase them out of their houses, bring in the cart, and take whatever we can.

English_display: While you were slacking off somewhere, we dealt with those peasants our own way. I can still hear them screaming and begging for mercy, heh heh!

English_reference: That can happen when we take our eyes off them, and then blood flows. But usually not ours, he he.
English_display: That'll only happen if we take our eyes off them. Then there might be bloodshed, but usually not ours. Heh heh!

English_reference: Come on the morrow. The sooner the better. I'd like to head out by noon. After that it makes no sense, and we’d only be rushing like mad.
English_display: Come back tomorrow, the sooner the better. We'll leave before noon, otherwise we'd only be in a rush.

English_reference: Which of us is in command here?
English_display: Which one of us is in charge here?

English_display: We haven't been to Bohunowitz in a while, I reckon they can't wait to see us.

English_display: You don't want a hungry army on your hands. The men turn into brutes who'll do whatever they can to get their hands on food. They'll kill, steal…

English_reference: Or else I’ll go alone, perhaps with a dumb Cuman for company and then you can be damn certain it won’t turn out well.
English_display: Or I'll go alone with a couple of thick-headed Cumans for company. Then you can be sure it won't turn out well.

English_reference: But fine, let’s go. Off to the horses!
English_display: But you're right, let's get going. Mount up!

English_reference: Let me tell you something. Either you come with me and you'll be able to watch out and make certain nothing happens to anyone, since you’re such a do-gooder.
English_display: Now listen up. Either you come and help me keep an eye on things, make sure nothing bad happens, since you're such a do-gooder.

English_reference: As you wish. If you change your mind, you know where to find me.
English_display: Suit yourself. If you change your mind, you know where to find me.

English_reference: Finally, they sent me someone who isn’t wet behind the ears and with straw sticking out of his boots.
English_display: Finally, they sent me someone who isn't wet behind the ears, and doesn't have straw sticking out of his boots.

English_reference: See how easy it is?
English_display: That wasn't so hard, was it?

English_reference: You don’t, eh? Now isn’t that nice! The whippersnapper doesn’t want to get his hands dirty.
English_display: You don't, eh? Now isn't that nice! His Grace doesn't want to get his hands dirty!

English_reference: Make your choice.
English_display: Take your pick.

English_reference: But we’re heading out in three days, with or without you.
English_display: But we're heading out in three days, with or without you.

English_display: What's it to be, longbow or crossbow?

English_display: But if you intend to beat everybody again like last time, watch out. No one will want to take you on if you win every time.

English_reference: One that you can shoot fast, mind! None of those siege beasts!
English_display: One that you can shoot fast, mind! None of them siege beasts!

English_display: You've come to win back the coin you lost here last time? I hope you've been practising, for your sake...

English_display: The winner's the one who knocks down the most straw birds. If there's a tie, whoever finishes shooting first wins.

English_display: Are you yanking my pizzle? You're telling me you didn't already know that?

English_display: Damn it! I don't think that'll work. You won't find an archer like that for miles.

English_display: It's actually pretty simple. You have to shoot down the straw birds on the range faster than your opponents.

English_display: Hmm, that's going to be tricky. Archers like that are hard to come by around here.

English_display: Do you want me to look around for beginners or more advanced archers? I might even find a few master sharpshooters around here for you!

English_display: Right, but these fellows ain't going to compete for nothing. Do you have the coin to stake?

English_reference: Mother of mercy, you see that...
English_display: Mother of God, look down upon me!

English_display: Look, I'll provide the arrows, I'll stick the birds on the range, but lend you a bow? That's asking a bit much...

English_display: If you miss, or you hit an opponent's target, all you get for that is egg on your face. Obviously.

English_display: I'm sorry to hear that, but not even a baby gets baptised for free..

English_display: You get your arrows, stand on the mark, and shoot down them straw birds I set up around the range as fast as you can.

English_reference: Memory like a sieve, eh?
English_display: Head like a sieve, eh?

English_display: Backing out at the last moment, are you? Well, I can't exactly force you, can I…?

English_display: Again? But you only finished shooting a while ago!

English_display: But you have to have one first!

English_display: Janosh… He is from Hungary. He speaks like a Tartar, but at least you can understand him a little, unlike Adder.

English_reference: Aye, if anyone's really unlucky, it's him.
English_display: Aye, if anyone is really unlucky, it is him.

English_display: Why? Good Lord! Such a question! They didn't ask us anything…

English_reference: I don't know what'll happen next…
English_display: I don't even know what'll happen next.

English_display: He's a damned good tailor. But besides that he does odd jobs around the village.

English_display: I'm so glad you'll help us.

English_display: The worst thing is the village paid some mercenaries for protection. But they took off the moment they saw horses kicking up dust on the horizon!

English_display: Mikush, Vendula and me all escaped at the last moment. The others… weren't so lucky.

English_reference: Alright then. If you change your mind… you know where to find me.
English_display: Alright then. If you change your mind, you know where to find me.

English_reference: If you're interested, you can challenge me. What it's going to be?
English_display: If you're interested, you can challenge me. What do you say?

English_reference: And if you don't... you drink!
English_display: And if you lose... you drink!

English_reference: But if you could  get a good look at it, you could bring it to me and leave Basan with a replica…
English_display: But if you could get a good look at it, you could bring it to me and leave Basan with a replica.

English_reference: As you wish. But if you change your mind, you know where to find  me…
English_display: As you wish. But if you change your mind, you know where to find me.

English_reference: As I said, I need you to bring something. Nobody must know and nobody must see you.
English_display: As I said, I need you to bring me something. Nobody must know and nobody must see you.

English_reference: How important is it for you when working… not to get… dirty?
English_display: How important is it for you when working to not get ... dirty?

English_reference: Well, what are you waiting for? Go make a copy and stick it in Basan's tent!
English_display: Well, what are you waiting for? Go make a replica and stick it in Basan's tent!

English_reference: Of course. Made of soft iron, with coloured glass instead of gemstones, just for looks.
English_display: Of course. Made of some soft iron, with coloured glass instead of gemstones, just for looks.

English_reference: You yourself must admit that such a weapon has no business being in the filthy paws of those pagans, why, they don't even know how to use it!
English_display: You yourself must admit that such a weapon has no business being in the filthy paws of those pagans, when they don't even know how to use it!

English_reference: I need you to bring me something. So that the owner of this item does not notice you have borrowed it.
English_display: I need you to bring me something. So that the owner of that thing does not notice you have borrowed it.

English_reference: Sorry boy, I need someone truly skilled, not some ragabash.
English_display: Sorry, lad. I need someone truly skilled, not just someone with a big mouth.

English_reference: You'll go to the tournament enclosure and on the left you will find his tent. It's white with green trim along the top.
English_display: You'll go to the tournament enclosure and on the left behind it, you will find his tent. It's white with green trim along the top.

English_reference: Now if I had a sword like that…
English_display: Now if I had a sword like that.

English_reference: For you? Nonsense!
English_display: You? Nonsense!

English_reference: If that means he’s happy to throw down coin for a bet, then yeah.
English_display: If that means he’s happy to throw down coin for a bet, then yes.

English_reference: That’s him to a tee – he promises you a mug of wine and before you blink, you’re in a wager over a whole bottle...
English_display: That’s him exactly – he promises you a mug of wine and before you blink, you’re in a wager over a whole bottle...

English_display: Some fellow called Raven from Bach runs the place. An honest sort.

English_display: That’s why I got into it too. It pays off better than those damned dice!

English_reference: I see you’re grabbing the chance by the scruff of the neck— I like that.
English_display: I see you’re grabbing the chance by the scruff of the neck - I like that.

English_display: We’ve got swords in the armoury we bought only recently, but truth be told they’re not much use already.

English_display: I know the guild prices and I can still do merchant maths, so I don’t need to ask.

English_reference: And when you walk by the pier where it all happened, you can still hear his giggling.
English_display: And when you walk by the pier where it all happened, you can still hear his chuckling.

English_reference: Feel free to look for it if you wish.
English_display: Look for yourself if you wish.

English_display: Maybe you would, but Matthias would never. He was an honest man, and with a big swing, he threw the silver axe back.

English_reference: I know stories so beautiful they would make a stone cry.
English_display: I could tell you stories so sad they'd make the Devil cry.

English_reference: But I can't just tell you… Now if you had some liquor or a few groschen, that might loosen my tongue.
English_display: But it's a lot of hard work for me… Now, if you had something to drink or a couple of groschen, that might help loosen my tongue.

English_reference: No problem, I have one like that. And it's much more interesting!
English_display: But it's not a problem, I have just the tale for you. And it's not one you'll hear from any priest!

English_display: Alright then. But if it's the one about the magic porridge pot, don't bother, I've heard it a hundred times.

English_display: Kuba, however, was not best pleased with his little brother's fortune. He deeply envied Matthias for his newfound wealth. So he set out to try the same thing.

English_reference: That's impossible! You're not just fucking with me, are you?
English_display: This can't be! You're not just yanking my pizzle, are you?

English_reference: The locals haven't had much appetite for the water sprite's treasures since then, but some still encounter him occasionally.
English_display: The locals have had no dealings with the water goblin since then, but some have had the bad luck to bump into him.

English_reference: Exactly, listen to this.
English_display: Well, quite. Listen on.

English_reference: Give your offering, Abraham!
English_display: A wise decision, friend!

English_reference: Aye, aye. Mathew was thinking the same thing…
English_display: Aye, and so did Matthias.

English_reference: So what's with the money? Do you have it or not?
English_display: So, let's talk money. Do you have it or not?

English_reference: Good choice. Nothing beats a good tearjerker.
English_display: Wise choice. Nothing better than a nice tragedy.

English_reference: Don't you worry, I've got just the story for you! I just hope you don't shit yourself.
English_display: Don't you worry, I've got just the one! I just hope you don't shit yourself with fear.

English_display: In haste, he began to search the muddy bed of the pond, and his hand soon touched something hard and heavy. He pulled it out and could not believe his eyes.

English_reference: But as far as I'm concerned, I'll just stay here with my liquor.
English_display: But leave me out of it, I'm fine here with my drink.

English_display: Story? What story? It's the truth!

English_display: One day, at the height of summer, they were working in the woods. The air was as hot as a furnace, so Matthias went to a nearby pond to cool himself.

English_reference: But the water sprite heard him, and he wasn't happy about it at all.
English_display: But the water goblin heard this shameful cry and was greatly upset by Kuba's greed.

English_display: If you want a story, pay up or get me something to drink.
